report.verdict: Lifecycle email and SMS for 410,000 subscribers stands out, as does the welcome series raising first-purchase rate. I’d write to you; the jobs show both campaign work and management.
write_up: You’re a marketing manager running lifecycle email and SMS for a camping gear brand, with earlier agency experience. The work is there, but the headline and About don’t yet do it justice.

The Fernhill welcome series is your best model: you name what you rebuilt and the change in first-purchase rate. Your earlier Fernhill job also gives a clear account of the move from Mailchimp to Klaviyo.

Start with the headline and About, using the lifecycle work and welcome series already in your current job. Then add the kinds of accounts and reports you supported at Lumen Street. A recruiter could understand your marketing work without having to dig for its strongest lines.

cards.line: Marketing Manager | Storyteller | Growth Mindset | Lifelong Learner
cards.cannot_tell: “Storyteller” and “Growth Mindset” could describe almost anyone. You run lifecycle email and SMS for a direct-to-consumer brand. Put that work beside your title.
cards.example: Marketing Manager | lifecycle email and SMS | direct-to-consumer camping gear
cards.question: What kinds of lifecycle campaigns do you run beyond the welcome series?

cards.line: Results-driven marketing professional with 8+ years of experience driving growth across multiple channels. Passionate about building brands people love and leading high-performing teams.
cards.cannot_tell: “Results-driven” leaves your best result out. The welcome series and its first-purchase rate are already in your Fernhill job. Bring them up here and tell the story in your own voice.
cards.example: I run lifecycle email and SMS for a direct-to-consumer camping gear brand with 410,000 subscribers. I rebuilt the welcome series from 3 emails to 7, raising first-purchase rate from 4.2% to 6.8% over two quarters.
cards.question: What did you change in the welcome series beyond the number of emails?

cards.line: Rebuilt the welcome series from 3 emails to 7, which raised first-purchase rate from 4.2% to 6.8% over two quarters.
cards.cannot_tell: This is the line to copy as a model. It names the work, the change and the period over which first-purchase rate rose.

cards.line: Supported client accounts and helped with reporting.
cards.cannot_tell: “Supported” and “helped” leave the account work unnamed. Which clients did you work with, and what went into the reports?
cards.example: Supported client accounts for [types of clients] and helped with [reports you prepared] [how often].
cards.question: What kinds of client accounts did you support, and which reports did you help prepare and how often?

cards.cannot_tell: Leadership is broad; your lifecycle email and SMS work tells a recruiter more about what you do. SMS is named in your current job but isn’t among the three skills shown.
cards.question: What kinds of SMS campaigns do you run?

fit.why: Your headline and current Fernhill job name you as a Marketing Manager, and the job describes lifecycle campaigns, a paid social budget and two specialists.
fit.level: manager, the Marketing Manager title and management of two marketing specialists
fit.note: “Marketing Manager” is in your headline and current title. “lifecycle email” and “SMS” are in your current job. “Klaviyo” is in your earlier Fernhill job. Recruiters may also search for segmentation, A/B testing and retention marketing; none appears on your profile. If they describe your work, add segmentation and A/B testing to the relevant job descriptions and retention marketing to the About. Move lifecycle email and SMS into the headline first.
